tldr_label: TL;DR — The Dow posts its best day of the year and oil sinks as Vance blames the Iran war for the midterm rout

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: The Dow jumped 3% to 53,356, its biggest gain of the year, after Trump accepted the election results. The S&P 500 rose 1.6%. [[TAG:success:Dow +3%]]

tldr_bullets.label: Oil
tldr_bullets.body: Oilprice.com reported that Brent fell about 9% toward $94 as Trump and Vance tied the Iran war to the Republican defeat and traders bet on a deal. [[TAG:warning:Brent ~$94]]

tldr_bullets.label: Congress
tldr_bullets.body: Democrats say lowering costs is their first priority, alongside investigations of the administration. Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi remain uncalled.

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: Vance said 'the reason we lost is the war'. Trump said he would do it again and threatened to 'finish the job' if Iran rejects a nuclear deal.

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: Eisenkot leads in recommendations as Herzog's consultations near an end. The haredi party UTJ declined to back Netanyahu.

tldr_bullets.label: World
tldr_bullets.body: Early results in South Africa show the ANC narrowly ahead of the DA. Zelensky says the Zaporizhzhia aid-center strike may have killed 70 people, a figure that is disputed.

sections.title: Wall Street Cheers Gridlock
sections.summary: The Dow posts its biggest gain of the year as Trump makes peace with the result; oil slides

paragraphs.heading: Rally
paragraphs.body: CBS News reported that the Dow jumped 1,569 points, or 3%, to 53,356.12, its biggest gain of the year, and that the S&P 500 rose about 1.6% and the Nasdaq 1.4%. CNBC said Trump's quick acceptance of the results drove the 'monster rally'. Analysts cited gridlock limiting big tax and spending bills. CBS said Trump Media fell nearly 25%. [[TAG:success:Dow +3%]]

paragraphs.heading: Oil
paragraphs.body: Oilprice.com reported that Brent first fell to about $100 on bets of a US-Iran deal, then dropped about 9% toward $94 as Trump and Vance blamed the war for the midterm losses. Fortune put Brent near $106 on Wednesday morning. Prices vary widely by timestamp. [[TAG:warning:oil volatile]]

paragraphs.heading: Asia
paragraphs.body: CNBC's live coverage reported that Korea's Kospi fell more than 5% on Thursday while other Asian markets were mixed. Benzinga said US futures were mixed after the rally.

sections.sources: CBS News, CNBC, Oilprice.com, Fortune, Benzinga

sections.title: The New Congress
sections.summary: Democrats put cutting costs first, alongside oversight; Alaska and Mississippi remain uncalled

paragraphs.heading: Agenda
paragraphs.body: Spectrum News reported that Schumer and Jeffries call cutting costs the first job of the new majority. ABC News and NBC News said Democrats also plan investigations of the administration. Their priorities include restoring health-care subsidies, reversing Medicaid cuts and challenging tariffs. Trump's veto still limits what can become law. [[TAG:info:affordability first]]

paragraphs.heading: Count
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that Alaska and Mississippi are the only Senate races the AP has not yet called. NBC Chicago reported a 54-44 Democratic Senate majority with those two pending. NBC News projected about 258 House seats for Democrats. In Alaska, Peltola and Sullivan are separated by a fraction of a point, and Roll Call reported that a judge dismissed a Justice Department suit seeking to block certification if Sullivan loses. [[TAG:warning:Alaska close]]

sections.title: Iran After the Vote
sections.summary: Vance blames the war for the GOP rout; Trump says he'd do it again and warns Tehran

paragraphs.heading: Blame
paragraphs.body: Military Times and NBC News reported that Vance wrote 'the reason we lost is the war', and Bloomberg said he also cited ties with Israel. ABC News reported that Trump said he would 'do it again', and Khaleej Times said Trump called the link to the war 'largely true'. ABC News added that its poll found voters more focused on the cost of living than on the war. [[TAG:warning:blame disputed]]

paragraphs.heading: Tehran
paragraphs.body: CBS News reported that Iran says the election shows Americans reject war. Fox News said Trump threatened to 'finish the job' if Iran rejects a nuclear deal, while the Revolutionary Guards vowed 'united' resistance. Gulf News reported that talks mediated by Qatar continue, with no decision on renewed strikes.

sections.title: Israel's Mandate
sections.summary: Eisenkot leads in recommendations as UTJ declines to back Netanyahu

paragraphs.heading: Recommendations
paragraphs.body: The Jerusalem Post reported that Religious Zionism and Shas recommended Netanyahu, while Yisrael Beytenu backed Eisenkot. The Times of Israel said the haredi faction UTJ will not recommend Netanyahu. Reports put Eisenkot at 56 or more recommendations to Netanyahu's 53 before the Joint List decides. The Tribune and JNS reported that consultations moved into a second day. The Knesset convenes on November 10. [[TAG:info:mandate pending]]

paragraphs.heading: US ties
paragraphs.body: The Times of Israel live blog reported that Eisenkot pledged after the US midterms to renew a bipartisan US-Israel alliance.

sections.title: Ukraine
sections.summary: Zelensky says the aid-center strike may have killed 70; Russia hits grids in nine regions

paragraphs.heading: Toll dispute
paragraphs.body: CBS News reported that Zelensky said Russia's 'insane attack' on an aid center in Zaporizhzhia region may have killed 70 people, and he pleaded for air defenses. ABC News reported 31 confirmed deaths, and Russia said the strike killed Ukrainian troops. [[TAG:warning:toll disputed]]

paragraphs.heading: Energy war
paragraphs.body: ABC News reported that Ukraine and Russia exchanged hundreds of drones overnight as Moscow kept targeting energy infrastructure, damaging facilities in nine regions. Al Jazeera reported that Ukrainian strikes killed three people in Russia's Belgorod region.

sections.title: Africa
sections.summary: Early count shows the ANC narrowly ahead of the DA in South Africa's local elections

paragraphs.heading: South Africa
paragraphs.body: CNBC Africa, citing Reuters, reported that with a quarter of votes counted the ANC had about 32% and the DA about 29%. Polity said the ANC narrowly leads, and Reuters noted the ANC would be about 14 points below its 2021 result if the trend holds. The DA leads in most Gauteng metros. The results are preliminary. [[TAG:warning:ANC near 32%]]

paragraphs.heading: Ebola
paragraphs.body: The Rio Times Africa brief reported 10,305 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,996 deaths in DR Congo as of October 28. UNICEF said it is stepping up preparedness in South Sudan, which has reported no cases.
